column4: dialect-gated per SUBTEST: a registeredBackends test, so it runs one subtest per dialect and mysql and mssql skip in these PostgreSQL-only jobs while postgres RUNS -- two, not three. Measured by name with only CLEAT_TEST_POSTGRES set, not derived from a delta. Guards cleat#1495: POST /api/schedules honours Idempotency-Key, so a retry is told apart from a genuine name collision instead of both being answered 409 schedule_exists. It has to run against a real database on every dialect because the discrimination is made in the store -- each has to recognise its own uniqueness violation and then ASK whether the key is held -- and because SQL Server is the only dialect where a unique index treats NULLs as equal, so an unfiltered index would refuse the SECOND keyless schedule and break creation for callers that never heard of idempotency.
